subject: Workplace Skills
title: Admitting Mistakes
description: Learn Admitting Mistakes in one minute.

hook.text: A CEO admitted to the entire company that her strategy was wrong. Trust scores jumped. She expected the opposite.

buildup.text: Leaders fear that admitting mistakes makes them look weak. In reality, it makes them look human and honest.

discovery.text: When leaders admit errors, it signals that truth matters more than ego. The team follows suit and stops hiding problems.

twist.text: An admission with a plan is powerful. 'I was wrong about X. Here's what I've learned and what we'll do differently.'

climax.text: Next time you're wrong, say it first. Don't wait for it to be discovered. Proactive honesty earns more respect.

punchline.text: Say it first. Owning mistakes builds more trust than hiding them.

quiz.question: Why does admitting mistakes increase a leader's credibility?
options: It lowers expectations for future performance
It signals truth matters more than ego, encouraging the team to be honest too
Employees feel sorry for the leader and work harder
